sermon.title: My Faith: The Source of Deception
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer opens “my faith” language from Revelation 2:13 and James 2:18, contrasts Christ’s faith with celebrities and politicians who invent their own beliefs, and teaches that the source of deception is not knowing God. From John 14, Jeremiah 4:22, John 8 and John 17:3 he shows eternal life is knowing the Father and Jesus, not merely believing about them.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: He cites Numbers 31:38 for “women that have not known a man”; the wording is Numbers 31:18 (linked as 31:18). Caption fixes include “my faith,” “Revelation,” “denied,” “Romans 1,” “homosexuality,” “1 Samuel 3:7,” and “John 14:8.” Sensitive content kept as spoken: named public figures (Bush, Obama, Romney, Maher, Oprah, Joseph Smith), homosexuality, Mormon practice, adultery, corrupt overseas ministers. Statistics (Oprah “10 or 18 years”) given as spoken and unchecked.

faqs.question: How many times is “I believe” used in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “I believe” is used five times: three about believing in Jesus as the Son of God who died for sins, and two about believing Jesus can do a miracle.

faqs.question: Does the Bible call itself a book of faith?
faqs.answer: He says nowhere does the Bible say it is a book of faith; it says it is a book of truth, and our faith should be in his truth and facts.

faqs.question: Does Romans 1 approve homosexual lifestyles?
faqs.answer: He says Obama called Romans 1 vague, but nothing is vague about Romans 1—it very clearly says it is wrong.

faqs.question: What does he say was the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah?
faqs.answer: He rejects the claim it was only inhospitality; Genesis says they were wicked and sinful, and one of those sins was homosexuality.

faqs.question: Is “unconditional love” in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says that statement is not in the Bible; there is a condition for God’s forgiveness and eternal life—you have to repent.

faqs.question: Can people who do not know God receive the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
faqs.answer: He says they cannot have the Comforter because they do not see God and do not know God.

faqs.question: What is the result of knowing God?
faqs.answer: He says the result of knowing him is keeping his word; Jesus kept the word of God.

faqs.question: Did Israel’s wilderness miracles mean they knew God?
faqs.answer: He says they had the fire, cloud and voice of God yet did not know God and did not obey him; presence and miracles are not his approval.

faqs.question: Did Samuel know the Lord while growing up in the temple?
faqs.answer: From 1 Samuel 3:7, even as a grown man raised in God’s house, Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word revealed to him.

scriptures.text_nkjv: (Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, nor was the word of the LORD yet revealed to him.)

faqs.question: Did Philip fully know Jesus after three years?
faqs.answer: Jesus asked Philip whether after so long he still had not known him, even after watching demons cast out, healings and the gospel preached.
